Mr. Ravi Bisht, Advocate, holding
brief of Mr. Aditya Pratap Singh,
Advocate for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Manoj Kumar, Standing
Counsel for the Union of India.
3. Petitioner participated in a selection
for admission in 8th standard in
Rashtriya Indian Military College (RIMC),
Dehradun. Since he was not allotted any
seat, therefore, he filed this writ petition
in April, 2026, seeking the following
reliefs:-
"i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Mandamus directing the Rashtriya Indian Military
College (Respondent No. 2 herein) to fill the
remaining one vacant seat for the January 2026
session strictly in accordance with the All India
Merit List.
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Mandamus directing the Respondents to consider
and grant admission to the Petitioner Khushal,
being next in order of merit, against the available
vacant seats.
iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Mandamus directing the Respondents to act in a
fair, transparent, and merit-based manner, and
not to leave seats vacant when eligible candidates
are available."
4. A counter affidavit is filed by Rakesh
Kumar, Assistant Administrative and
Training Officer, RIMC, Dehradun. Para
14 of the said counter affidavit is
extracted below:-
"14. That the paragraph No. 11 of of the Writ Petition
is wrong and admitted as stated. It is wrong to say
that 36 seats have to be filled in each term. It is

submitted that the number of vacancies in each term
is determined by the Army Training Command which
prescribed 25 boys and 10 girls for the term
commencing in Jan 2026. It is relevant to mention
that the total authorized strength for girl cadets is
now 50 in addition to 250 boy cadets. Separate
arrangements are being made for accommodating girl
cadets who have secured admission to RIMC starting
from Jan 2024, and in respect of whom the Hon'ble
Supreme Court of India has passed an order directing
the higher authorities of the Respondent No. 2 to
make provision for accommodating 100 girls cadets.
The financial, administrative and logistical
parameters for complying with the directions of the
Apex Court are being worked out by the Government
of India in consultation with the Ministry of Defence,
HQ Army Training Command (ARTRAC) and RIMC,
and have yet to be finalized and implemented. Based
on the above, vacancy of 25 boys and 10 girls was
approved within the framework of the infrastructural
and logistical facilities available at RIMC including
the classroom strength. It is reiterated that the
admission notification issued by RIMC which the
Petitioner mentions in this paragraph of the Writ
Petition, by no stretch of imagination confers any
right upon the Petitioner to secure admission to RIMC.
It is wrong to say that the Petitioner cleared all the
procedural requirements. It is wrong to say that RIMC
was bound to take 36 admissions. All the vacancies
as prescribed have been duly filled and the rank of
the Petitioner is next in the order of merit in the All
India Merit List. The candidate Avneet Thakur who
left RIMC after joining had a score of 303.83 marks
and the next candidate in the All India Merit List ie.
Rishabh with a score of 302 marks was selected with
regard to the candidate Shubham Swarup Das who
also left after joining had a score of 290.25 marks
and the next candidate in the All India Merit List was
Dhruv Bahuguna with score of 285.25 marks who
was selected. The Petitioner with 282.25 marks is
next in the All India Merit List."
5. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing
Counsel appearing for respondents
submits that there were only 35
vacancies available in 8th standard in
RIMC and petitioner stood 36 in order of
merit. He submits that as per policy,
only one seat was earmarked for
candidates belonging to Haryana State
and that seat was already filled by
admission to a student from State of
Haryana, therefore, there was no
vacancy left for the petitioner. He further
submits that academic session in RIMC

starts in the month of January and the
academic session is now over. He thus
submits that the writ petition has
become infructuous.
6. This Court do not find any scope for
interference in the matter, as there is no
one, who scored lower marks than
petitioner and was admitted.
7. Since all the available vacancies
were supplied by giving admission to
students, who scored higher marks,
therefore, the grievance raised by
petitioner is without any substance.
8. The writ petition is, accordingly,
dismissed.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 17.08.2026
Navin
